Resolves #18950

Related: #18762 · #18943

🪢 *Under a column-selecting model, one Tab inside a cell edit left the highlighted column a column behind the selected cell — for good, because the arrow keys step the column from wherever it is.*

Was a draft stacked on #18943 (same block of `CellEditing#startEdit`). That PR merged; this is now one commit, `4489725e31`, on `dev` including #18955.

## What changes

`CellEditing#startEdit`: a model that selects columns follows the edit by its column — `setSelectedColumns([dataField])`, the absolute setter a cell click uses. Every start passes there (Enter, F2, a double-click, Tab's target), so the column is right for as long as the edit lasts and wherever it ends. The setter repaints nothing when the column is selected already.

Evidence: L3 (real Chromium, real keys and pointer, CI-executed e2e tier) → L3 required (AC-1…AC-4). Residual: none.

agent-preflight: not hosted here; the PR baseline jobs run in CI. Change class: restoration (`fix`).
